items.title: Fortnite Will Give Kids What They've Always Wanted: AI Pride And Prejudice Fan Fic
items.excerpt: Neal Stephenson's company Whenere is bringing an AI-driven storytelling platform to Fortnite
items.rationale: New launch: Neal Stephenson's Whenere is bringing an AI-driven narrative platform into Fortnite. That puts generative storytelling inside the largest UGC game ecosystem, which matters to narrative and level designers.

items.title: Original DOOM Gets NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering Through a Custom DirectX 12 Port
items.excerpt: Developer Nikolai Zhivotenko ports DOOM to Windows with NVIDIA DLSS 5 Neural Rendering, enhancing its graphics through modern upscaling techniques.
items.rationale: A new release: a custom DX12 port that applies DLSS 5 neural rendering to the original DOOM's sprite art. It is a concrete test of what the AI filter does to classic pixel art.

items.title: The OG Crash Team Racing for PS1 just arrived on PC, but it's sadly yet another recomp spoiled by AI
items.rationale: A new release: a PC recompilation of PS1 Crash Team Racing built with AI. It is the latest flashpoint in the preservation community's fight over vibe-coded ports.

items.title: Artist Falsely Accused Of Using GenAI Gives The Perfect Response, 'Don't Forget What Makes Us Human!'
items.excerpt: Loish took to Instagram to explain why such accusations matter, and how to spot original creativity
items.rationale: Illustrator Loish answers false gen-AI accusations and explains how to recognise original work. This hits artists directly: their process and style are now under suspicion by default.

items.title: "A creative idea can save more money than AI can right now" – Glen Schofield on his retirement, Callisto Protocol's development, and the state of AAA
items.excerpt: The Call of Duty and Dead Space alumnus explains why he doesn't view AI as a tool and why he isn't a fan of remote work
items.rationale: Dead Space and Callisto Protocol creator Glen Schofield argues that creative ideas cut AAA costs more than AI does today. It is a senior creative director's counterweight to studios' AI-efficiency pitch.

dedup.note: Pool: 10 items. Dropped all three Google Playground items in cluster c1: Game Developer, 80 Level and Eurogamer, which pairs Google Playground with Unity Spark. The 10-08 games run already published this launch as the 80.lv Unity Spark card and explicitly folded Google Playground into it (Unity Spark is the prompting tool built for Playground). Any of the three would repeat that story. Dropped GamingBolt 'Capcom has no plans for gen-AI assets in RE Engine': it carries a related history_match to The Verge Capcom story from 10-05 and is a clarification of that same statement with no new release. The 10-08 run rejected IGN's version of it for the same reason. Dropped PC Gamer 'haystack slop' (09-28): a stale weekly Steam roundup with a related history_match to the GamesRadar 'Robloxification of Steam' story from 09-27. No funding or exec items in the pool. The DOOM DLSS 5 port is a distinct new port release, not commentary on the running DLSS 5 story. The CTR recomp is a different release from the Banjo-Tooie recomp published 10-03. The pool had exactly 5 fresh items, so all 5 were taken with no backfill reserve. Diversity: 5 distinct outlets (Aftermath, Wccftech, GamesRadar+, Kotaku, GamesIndustry.biz), and accents are distinct across the single games category.
